overview.text: The King Brown (Mulga) Snake is Australia's largest venomous land snake. Despite its name it belongs to the black snakes and is only distantly related to true brown snakes.

identification.text: Robust, with a head slightly wider than the body and prominent cheeks.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Can reach 2 to 2.5 m and 3 to 6 kg; the longest confirmed was 3.3 m. Males are bigger.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: All Australian states except Victoria and Tasmania - most of northern, western and central Australia.

behaviour.text: Mostly active at dusk, resting in soil cracks, burrows or under rocks and logs; in warm months it is active later into the night. Males wrestle in the breeding season.

recognise.text: Large, heavy brown snake with a broad head.
